transcript: We're in an age of perpetual disaster and Weather Girl perfectly captures that 2025 existential dread. This new play by Brian Watkins starring Julia McDermott is about a weather girl in California who, after reporting from the front lines of a wildfire with a plastered smile on her face, reaches a breaking point. She recounts the following few days which are blurry and nothing short of absurd. Elements of her story feel pretty far fetched, but there's a sense of dissociation or indifference that almost makes you have to believe it's real. And you have to lock in because you never really know where it's going. This piece surprised me — I thought it was going to be a much messier exploration of inner mayhem based on that hilarious marketing image, but it's much more subtle, which arguably makes it more resonant. The concept of the weather girl perfectly captures how we all tuck away our existential dread before we go out into the world each day, while the world around us burns. All that's to say, if you're looking for a silly and entertaining romp, this is not that. It’s strange and twisty, to the point where I wasn't sure how much I was enjoying it throughout the performance, but as soon as it ended and started to settle in my mind, it hit me and I think it's one of the smartest pieces I've seen in recent memory. Weather Girl is running in Brooklyn at St Ann's Warehouse. With that, another program for my collection.
